descs.t: Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens has endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for the US Senate over her party's nominee, Abdul El-Sayed, days before the vote. Stevens, who took 47.55% in the Democratic primary, appeared with Rogers at a Detroit church. We walk through what she said, how Democrats reacted and what it could mean on Tuesday.

Haley Stevens, the pro-Israel Democrat who lost the Michigan Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, is now backing Republican Mike Rogers, saying we can't stand with hate. Hakeem Jeffries and Ayanna Pressley have lined up behind El-Sayed, while President Trump says he would love to have her. We break down why she crossed over and whether it moves the race.

A Democrat who took nearly half the primary vote in Michigan just stood beside the Republican and told voters to back him. Haley Stevens says she cannot stand with hate; her own party calls it betrayal. We look at the fight inside the Democratic Party and what it means for the Senate on Tuesday.

intro.plain: Big news out of Michigan. Haley Stevens, the Democrat who lost the Senate primary to Abdul El-Sayed, has endorsed Republican Mike Rogers, and she did it standing next to him at a Detroit church. The vote is Tuesday. Her party is furious and Trump says he would love to have her. So chat, does this move votes in Michigan, or is it noise?
intro.mid: Three days before Michigan votes, the Democrat who almost won the Senate primary just endorsed the Republican. Haley Stevens says she can't stand with hate and is backing Mike Rogers over Abdul El-Sayed. Democrats are lining up to call it betrayal, Trump is inviting her into the GOP. Chat, was she right to cross over, or did she just burn her career?
intro.bold: Haley Stevens walked into a Detroit church this morning next to Mike Rogers and told Michigan to vote Republican. A Democrat who took 47.55% in her own party's primary. She says she can't stand with hate. Her party says traitor. Trump says welcome. Chat, one question: if you were a Michigan Democrat, would her endorsement change your vote on Tuesday?

hook.plain: Days before the vote, Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for Senate. Here is what she said, and how her party answered.
hook.mid: She nearly won the Democratic primary. Now Haley Stevens is campaigning for the Republican. Here is why, and whether it moves Michigan.

descs.t: Poland is in a constitutional crisis over who controls its Constitutional Tribunal. Prime Minister Donald Tusk moved to appoint new judges, while President Karol Nawrocki stood with the court's suspended leadership, and the EU says Poland's parliament must have the right to appoint judges. We walk through what happened, who did what, and where it goes next.

Donald Tusk says he will rebuild Poland's constitutional court; his critics call his move a coup backed by Brussels. President Karol Nawrocki warns he will never let the EU take powers from Poland, and Marine Le Pen has joined the alarm. We break down the claims on both sides and what this fight means for the rule of law in Poland.

Critics say Donald Tusk sent riot police to seat his own judges on Poland's top court, with the EU cheering him on. President Karol Nawrocki is fighting back. Is this reform or a power grab? We go through the claims, the reports and what is at stake for a free Poland.

intro.plain: Let's go to Poland, where the government and the president are locked in a fight over the country's top court. Prime Minister Donald Tusk moved to appoint new judges to the Constitutional Tribunal, President Nawrocki backed the court's suspended leadership, and the EU has taken Tusk's side. So chat, who should get to appoint the judges in Poland?
intro.mid: Poland is in a full constitutional crisis. Donald Tusk wants his own judges on the Constitutional Tribunal, President Nawrocki is physically backing the old leadership, and Brussels says parliament must decide. Critics are calling it a coup, Tusk calls it rebuilding the court. Chat, reform or power grab?
intro.bold: Critics are calling it a coup. Reports say riot police, judges being swapped on Poland's top court, and the EU cheering Donald Tusk on while President Nawrocki tells Brussels Poland will never hand over its powers. Marine Le Pen is sounding the alarm. Chat, straight question: is Tusk saving Poland's courts or seizing them?
